title: Design contract
description: Output of the Design stage, on UI work only. The spec, the mock, the lock, and the build brief written from the locked mock. A contract that fails this schema is a hard stop, not a warning. The next stage never runs on it.

run_id.description: The run folder under .hyperpower/runs/. null when the stage ran without a run journal.

prompt_hash.description: sha256 of the prompt that produced this contract. The orchestrator stamps it, so it is absent on the contract a stage hands to hp-validate. /hyperpower:resume reads it.

cache_key.description: Stamped by hp-journal after validation. hp-journal owns this shape, so the schema records that the field is legal and checks nothing inside it.

recorded_at.description: Stamped by hp-journal when it writes the step file, so it is absent on the contract a stage hands to hp-validate.

files_read.description: Every path this stage read. /hyperpower:resume re-hashes this list to detect drift. A file read and left out is drift the resume check cannot see.

assumptions.description: Every fact this stage relied on that it did not read in front of it. Present even when empty: an absent array reads to /hyperpower:why as zero assumptions declared. Carry an upstream assumption forward with its original id, claim and declared_at.

id.description: Unique within the run, not within the step. a1, a2.

claim.description: The fact relied on, in one sentence.

declared_at.description: The step that first declared it.

checkable.description: The file path or command that settles the claim later. null when nothing settles it, which stamps the status unresolved.

status.description: declared until the gate-time pass re-reads checkable and stamps it.

rejected.description: Designs considered and dropped. /hyperpower:why --rejected reads this array by name and prints option and reason, so it is flat and top level.

notes.description: Anything the next stage needs. Never shaped and never capped.

routes.description: The routes this surface lives at. The caller passes one of them to hp-gates --route per gate invocation, which is what fills {route} for the browser, a11y and visual gates.

spec.description: All four lists. A spec with only the happy state produces a mock with only the happy state.

states.description: Every state the surface can be in.

data.description: Each field shown: its source, its type, and what renders when it is absent.

interactions.description: Each control, what it does, and what it shows while it is doing it.

edge_cases.description: The values that break the layout.

mock.description: null when status is blocked and no mock was built.

sha.description: git hash-object of the mock file.

self_contained.description: No network request, script, font or remote image.

locked.description: True only when a human locked this mock. locked true with lock.locked_by null is a contradiction, so never write that pair. A headless run writes false.

lock.description: A mock nobody clicked is a proposal, not a contract. Never locked for it.

rounds.description: Three maximum. A fourth means the spec was wrong.

spec_superseded.description: Where the mock and the spec differ, the mock wins. The recorded disagreement tells the next reader which one decided.

build_brief.description: Written from the locked mock, not from the spec. Every row cites the mock.

element.description: What it is, in the mock's own words.

selector.description: The id or selector in the mock file.

source_component.description: The existing component to reuse, or null for new.

tokens.description: The repo's own colours, spacing and type scale. Never an invented palette.

routes.description: The routes the visual gate checks. Same list as the top-level routes.

baseline_valid.description: False for an unlocked mock, so the visual gate has the fact and not an inference.
